# Tracking down a race condition before a team demo

[Behavioral](../README.md) · [Home](../../README.md)

> **One-line hook:** "Two days before our capstone demo, about 1 in 20 orders in our app were silently disappearing, and I took ownership of finding out why."

_Sample story showing the format; replace it with your own._

| | |
|---|---|
| **Situation** | Final-year capstone: a 4-person team building a food-ordering web app (React + Flask + Postgres). 48 hours before the demo to faculty and an industry sponsor, testers reported that some orders never appeared in the kitchen view. |
| **Task** | Nobody could reproduce it reliably and the team was splitting up to polish the UI. I volunteered to own the bug end to end, because a missing-orders bug in a live demo would sink the project. |
| **Action** | 1. **Reproduced it:** wrote a 30-line script firing 200 concurrent orders and got the loss rate to about 5%, so it was load-related, not random. 2. **Isolated it:** added request-ID logging and found two requests reading the same "next order number" before either wrote it, a read-then-write race. 3. **Fixed it:** replaced the app-side counter with a Postgres `SEQUENCE` and wrapped order creation in one transaction. 4. **Prevented regressions:** added the concurrency script to CI and walked the team through the failure in a 10-minute session. |
| **Result** | 0 lost orders across 5,000 concurrent test orders; the demo ran cleanly, and the sponsor asked about our testing approach. The CI check caught a similar issue two weeks later. |
| **Learned** | Reproduce first, guess later. I now design stateful endpoints with concurrency in mind from day one and ask "what if two of these run at once?" in code reviews. |

## Fits these questions

- What is the hardest bug you have fixed? (**challenge**)
- Tell me about a time you took ownership. (**ownership**)
- Tell me about working under a tight deadline. (**deadline**)
- How did you help your team succeed? (**teamwork**)

## Likely follow-ups

<details><summary>Q: Why not just add a lock in the application?</summary>

A: There were multiple app workers (gunicorn processes), so an in-process lock would not work across them; the database is the single source of truth, and a sequence is atomic there.

</details>

<details><summary>Q: What would you do differently?</summary>

A: Add load testing earlier: the bug existed for three weeks before anyone generated real concurrency.

</details>

<details><summary>Q: How did the team react when you took it on?</summary>

A: Relieved, but I made sure not to disappear: a short status update every few hours, so the UI work could be reprioritised if I did not find it.

</details>

A review means telling it out loud in 2 to 3 minutes without notes (`prep start star-race-condition-team-project`).
